     9	# instead of failing the run. The value fills `image_digest` in host mode and
    10	# `fingerprint` in every mode (MANIFEST.json, pipeline.json, runs.jsonl). It reads the
    11	# HOST toolchain: in container mode the phases run on the image's toolchain, and the
    12	# image digest (not this value) identifies the batch's versions (on 2026-10-15 the host

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Probe ablation-row.sh builder with edge inputs. Creates fresh copies only; deletes nothing.
export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"
cd "$HOME/head-row" || exit 1
ROW="$PWD/evals/harness/ablation-row.sh"
FX="$PWD/evals/tests/fixtures/ablation-runs"
P="$HOME/probe/$(date +%s)"
mkdir -p "$P"
echo "probe dir $P; jq $(jq --version)"
mk() { cp -a "$FX/runs/a1-build" "$P/$1"; }
go() { local n="$1"; shift; out="$("$ROW" --run-dir "$P/$n" --task-yaml "$FX/tasks/bf-01/task.yaml" "$@" 2>&1)"; rc=$?; printf '%-40s rc=%s  %s\n' "$n" "$rc" "$(printf '%s' "$out" | head -c 300)"; }
ENV="sandbox/grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-1/adversarial-review.json"
mk g1; echo '{"recall": 0.5, "hidden_tests": null}' > "$P/g1/grade.json"; go g1
mk g2; echo '{"verdict_accuracy_per_gate": "x"}' > "$P/g2/grade.json"; go g2
mk g3; : > "$P/g3/grade.json"; go g3
mk g4; echo '[1]' > "$P/g4/grade.json"; go g4
mk g5; echo '"str"' > "$P/g5/grade.json"; go g5
mk g6; echo '{"hidden_tests": "7/8"}' > "$P/g6/grade.json"; go g6
mk g7; echo '{"false_positives": {"n": 1}}' > "$P/g7/grade.json"; go g7
mk g8; echo '{"regressions": 2, "verdict": "APPROVED"}' > "$P/g8/grade.json"; go g8
mk e1; jq '.metadata = "x"' "$FX/runs/a1-build/$ENV" > "$P/e1/$ENV"; go e1
mk e2; jq '.verdict_quality = "DEGRADED"' "$FX/runs/a1-build/$ENV" > "$P/e2/$ENV"; go e2
mk e3; echo '{"verdict_quality":{"voices_planned":"2","voices_succeeded":1}}' > "$P/e3/$ENV"; go e3
mk m1; echo '{"primitive_id":"MODELINV","payload":"oops"}' > "$P/m1/eval/model-invoke.jsonl"; go m1
mk m2; printf '%s\n' '{"primitive_id":"MODELINV","payload":{"effort_effective":"high","calling_primitive":"x"}}' > "$P/m2/eval/model-invoke.jsonl"
"$ROW" --run-dir "$P/m2" --task-yaml "$FX/tasks/bf-01/task.yaml" | jq -c '["m2 (payload.effort absent -> falls back to phase effort_requested)", .degraded, .degraded_reason]'
mk p1; jq '.started = ""' "$FX/runs/a1-build/meta/pipeline.json" > "$P/p1/meta/pipeline.json"; go p1
mk p2; jq '.started = "2026-10-22T18:18:43.123456Z" | .finished = "2026-10-22T18:18:45+00:00"' "$FX/runs/a1-build/meta/pipeline.json" > "$P/p2/meta/pipeline.json"; go p2
mk p3; jq '.phases[2].models_used = {}' "$FX/runs/a1-build/meta/pipeline.json" > "$P/p3/meta/pipeline.json"
"$ROW" --run-dir "$P/p3" --task-yaml "$FX/tasks/bf-01/task.yaml" | jq -r '"p3 empty models_used degraded=\(.degraded)"'
mk p4; jq '.phases[2].model_requested = null' "$FX/runs/a1-build/meta/pipeline.json" > "$P/p4/meta/pipeline.json"
"$ROW" --run-dir "$P/p4" --task-yaml "$FX/tasks/bf-01/task.yaml" | jq -c '["p4 model_requested null",.degraded,.degraded_reason]'
mk p5; jq '.status = "weird"' "$FX/runs/a1-build/meta/pipeline.json" > "$P/p5/meta/pipeline.json"
"$ROW" --run-dir "$P/p5" --task-yaml "$FX/tasks/bf-01/task.yaml" > "$P/p5.jsonl"; jq -r '"p5 status=\(.status)"' "$P/p5.jsonl"; "$ROW" --validate "$P/p5.jsonl" --allow-ungraded; echo "p5 validate rc=$?"
mk p6; jq 'del(.phases[2].modelinv_lines)' "$FX/runs/a1-build/meta/pipeline.json" > "$P/p6/meta/pipeline.json"; go p6 | cut -c1-100
mk p7; jq '.phases[2].verdict = "none"' "$FX/runs/a1-build/meta/pipeline.json" > "$P/p7/meta/pipeline.json"
"$ROW" --run-dir "$P/p7" --task-yaml "$FX/tasks/bf-01/task.yaml" | jq -c '["p7 phase verdict none passes through:", [.phases[]|select(.label=="REVIEW")][0].verdict]'
mk t1; : > "$P/t1.yaml"; "$ROW" --run-dir "$P/t1" --task-yaml "$P/t1.yaml" 2>&1 | head -c 200; echo " | t1 (empty task.yaml) rc=${PIPESTATUS[0]}"
mk mf; : > "$P/mf.json"; "$ROW" --run-dir "$P/mf" --task-yaml "$FX/tasks/bf-01/task.yaml" --manifest "$P/mf.json" 2>&1 | head -c 200; echo " | mf (empty manifest) rc=${PIPESTATUS[0]}"
mk a1; echo '{"arm_map":{"abl-fixture-a1_full-bf-01-t1":"a0_bare"}}' > "$P/a1.json"; mv "$P/a1/meta/arm" "$P/a1/meta/arm.moved"
"$ROW" --run-dir "$P/a1" --task-yaml "$FX/tasks/bf-01/task.yaml" --manifest "$P/a1.json" | jq -r '"a1 manifest(a0_bare) vs pipeline.json(a1_full), no meta/arm -> arm=\(.arm) (no refusal)"'
echo "--- attempts edge:"
"$ROW" --run-dir "$P/a1" --task-yaml "$FX/tasks/bf-01/task.yaml" --attempts 007 | jq -c '"attempts 007 -> \(.attempts)"'
"$ROW" --run-dir "$P/a1" --task-yaml "$FX/tasks/bf-01/task.yaml" --attempts 0 | jq -c '"attempts 0 -> \(.attempts)"'
echo "--- jq 1.6 run of the builder:"
PATH="/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/local/bin" "$ROW" --run-dir "$FX/runs/a1-build" --task-yaml "$FX/tasks/bf-01/task.yaml" 2>&1 | head -c 400; echo " | jq16 rc=${PIPESTATUS[0]}"
echo "--- jq 1.6 run of --validate:"
"$ROW" --run-dir "$FX/runs/a1-build" --task-yaml "$FX/tasks/bf-01/task.yaml" > "$P/ok.jsonl"
PATH="/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/local/bin" "$ROW" --validate "$P/ok.jsonl" --allow-ungraded; echo "jq16 validate rc=$?"
echo "--- --out lock file left behind?"; "$ROW" --run-dir "$FX/runs/a1-build" --task-yaml "$FX/tasks/bf-01/task.yaml" --out "$P/out/r.jsonl"; ls "$P/out"
echo "--- help:"; "$ROW" --help | head -3; echo "help rc=${PIPESTATUS[0]}"

I have everything I need; nothing further to request. Here is the review of the "rows" slice.

## What I ran

- `bash -n` on `ablation-row.sh` and `regen.sh`: clean. `shellcheck` is not installed here.
- **bats, as shipped** (fresh copy of `pr/head`, jq 1.6 or 1.7 — irrelevant): **0/18 pass**. Every test dies in `setup()` at `cp -a "$FX/runs"` because the PR contains no `evals/tests/fixtures/ablation-runs/runs/` directory.
- **regen.sh under jq 1.6** (system `/usr/bin/jq`): every `pipeline-run.sh` invocation exits 2 with a jq compile error (`{label: $label, ...}` at pipeline-run.sh:708), yet regen prints `wrote 10 run directories` and **exits 0**. Running the bats against those broken fixtures: 11/18 pass, 7 fail.
- **regen.sh under jq 1.7.1** (downloaded into `~/.local/bin`, which regen.sh hard-sets in PATH): all runs succeed; **bats 18/18 pass**.
- `--validate` probes (26 hand-crafted rows) and builder probes (~20 malformed grade/envelope/MODELINV/pipeline inputs) — details below.
- Shape comparison of `pipeline-run.sh`'s `write_pipeline` (:318-341) and per-phase record (:821-849) against what the row reads.

## Findings

**1. The fixture run directories the tests depend on are not in the PR**
`head/evals/tests/ablation-row.bats:19` — `cp -a "$FX/runs" "$T/runs"`
Severity: high. Confidence: high (PR.md says 72 files; `head/` has exactly 72; none under `ablation-runs/runs/`; same line at `took-effect.bats:18`).
Scenario: CI's `bats --print-output-on-failure evals/tests/` (`bats-tests.yml:221`) runs this file; all 18 tests fail with `cp: cannot stat '.../ablation-runs/runs': No such file or directory`. No workflow step runs `regen.sh` first. Either the directory must be committed, or `setup()` must build it (and then the bats header's claim at lines 8-9 that the fixtures are checked-in "real pipeline-run.sh runs" is wrong).

**2. Row builder does not compile under jq 1.6**
`head/evals/harness/ablation-row.sh:285` — `phases: [ $phases[] | {name, label, session_id, model_requested, ...`
Severity: medium. Confidence: high (reproduced: `jq: error: syntax error, unexpected ',', expecting ':'` → script exits 3, no row).
`label` is a jq keyword; the `{label}` shorthand is only accepted from jq 1.7. Nothing in the repo pins jq ≥ 1.7 (fingerprint.sh:75 only records the version). `--validate` works on 1.6. Write `"label": .label`.

**3. regen.sh swallows pipeline failures and exits 0 with broken fixtures**
`head/evals/tests/fixtures/ablation-runs/regen.sh:63` — `... > "$GEN/last.log" 2>&1 || { rc=$?; sed -n "1,20p" "$GEN/last.log" >&2; }`
Severity: medium. Confidence: high (observed: 9 runs exit 2, `regen: wrote 10 run directories`, exit 0; grade.json then written onto failed runs; MANIFEST.json rewritten).
Only `refused-a4-review` is expected to be non-zero (a refusal). Any other non-zero should abort regen, otherwise a maintainer commits fixtures with `status: infrastructure_error` and empty `phases` and the suite silently loses coverage (11/18 still passed on those fixtures, including test 17 "every fixture run yields a valid row").

**4. Scalar `recall` in grade.json aborts the row**
`head/evals/harness/ablation-row.sh:266` — `($rc.defects_seeded // $rc.seeded // $rc.total // null)` (also :267, :298, :300)
Severity: medium. Confidence: medium (concrete failing input `{"recall": 0.5}` → `Cannot index number with "defects_seeded"`, exit 5, no row; whether Sprint 259's grader will emit a scalar is unknown — the script already hedges across three key spellings, so the shape is clearly not settled).

**5. Non-object nested fields in untrusted inputs crash the builder (exit 5, undocumented)**
Severity: medium. Confidence: high (each reproduced).
- `:235` `companion_planned: e.metadata.companion_voice.planned` — envelope with `"metadata": "x"` → `Cannot index string with "companion_voice"`.
- `:232-234` `e.verdict_quality.voices_planned` — envelope with `"verdict_quality": "DEGRADED"` → crash. `envelope()` at :203 only checks the top level is an object.
- `:305`/`:307` `$g.verdict_accuracy_per_gate.review` — grade with `"verdict_accuracy_per_gate": "x"` → crash.
- `:239`/`:242` `.payload.effort_effective` — MODELINV row with `"payload": "oops"` → crash.
- `:262` `($g.contaminated // null)` — grade.json that parses as `[1]` or `"str"` → crash (only pipeline.json is checked for `type == "object"` at :162).
Envelopes and MODELINV rows are written inside the agent sandbox (CLAUDE.md: treat as UNTRUSTED), so one malformed file loses the run's row and the batch runner gets exit 5, which is not one of the documented 0/1/2.

**6. Empty grade.json / MANIFEST.json produce a jq usage error instead of a usage message**
`head/evals/harness/ablation-row.sh:171` — `GRADE_JSON="$(jq -c '.' "$GRADE")" || usage ...` (same at :176)
Severity: low. Confidence: high. `jq -c .` on an empty file exits 0 with no output, so `--argjson g ""` fails at :225 with `jq: invalid JSON text passed to --argjson` (exit 2 only by coincidence).

**7. Unknown pipeline status strings pass straight into the row**
`head/evals/harness/ablation-row.sh:260` — `($p.status // "infrastructure_error" | if . == "running" then "interrupted" else . end)`
Severity: low. Confidence: high (`status: "weird"` → row `status: "weird"`, caught only by a later `--validate`). Documented derivation names five pipeline statuses; anything else should map to `infrastructure_error` or be refused, since `--status` is already validated against the enum at :164.

**8. `--validate` soft spots** (each verified with a crafted row that passed)
`head/evals/harness/ablation-row.sh:105` — `need("schema_version"; num)` accepts `2`.
`:117-118` — `status: "contaminated"` with `contaminated: null` is accepted; `degraded: false` with a non-null `degraded_reason` is accepted (:123 is one-directional).
No range checks (`hidden_test_pass_rate: 7` passes). Severity: low. Confidence: high. Everything else I threw at it was rejected correctly: `status=running`, string `phases[0].exit`, `degraded` without reason, string/array `phases`, non-string snapshot, bad verdict enum, string `voices_run`, missing nested `dot_claude_writes`, null `agy_opt_in`, wrong types on every field in `phases[1]`, invalid JSON line (reported with the correct line number), no trailing newline. The `[need(...)][0] // ...` chain is sound: `need` emits only non-null strings, so no legitimate first element can short-circuit it. Verified under both jq 1.6 and 1.7.1.

**9. `ms()` only accepts `Z`-suffixed timestamps**
`head/evals/harness/ablation-row.sh:230` — `ts | sub("\\.[0-9]+Z$"; "Z") | fromdateiso8601 * 1000`
Severity: low. Confidence: low-impact/high-repro. `finished: "...+00:00"` or `started: ""` → `date ... does not match format`, exit 5. pipeline-run.sh always writes `%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ` (:295, :323) and sets `STARTED` before any `write_pipeline`, so this is only a robustness gap. Note the second-resolution stamps make `wall_clock_ms` a multiple of 1000 (fixture: 2000 ms vs Σ`wall_ms` ≈ 600 ms); fine for the suite's ±15 % rule.

**10. Fixture shape round-trips the stub's own assumptions for envelopes and MODELINV**
`head/evals/tests/fixtures/claude-stub-pipeline.sh:79-80` (envelope) and `:92-93` (MODELINV payload)
Severity: medium if wrong, Confidence: low (cannot verify — the real flatline-orchestrator and cheval emitters are not in the PR).
`verdict_quality.{status,voices_planned,voices_succeeded}`, `metadata.companion_voice.planned`, `payload.{calling_primitive,effort,effort_effective,cost_micro_usd}` are defined only by the stub written in this PR; `took-effect.sh` reads the same names, so the PR is internally consistent, but if the production names differ, `voices_run` is silently all-null and degraded causes (3) and (4) never fire — no error is raised. By contrast the **pipeline.json shape is genuinely verified**: fixtures are produced by the real `pipeline-run.sh`, and I compared field-by-field — `status`, `phases[].{name,label,skipped,modelinv_lines{from,to},models_used (object model→tokens),model_requested,effort_requested,refusal_fallbacks[],cost_usd,ledger_cost_usd,timed_out,wall_ms,duration_ms,snapshot,verdict,exit}`, `snapshots{implement,fix1,fix2}`, `cap_phase`, `started/finished`, `run_id`, `arm`, `trial` (number), `source_commit`, `fingerprint`, `image_digest`, `executor_mode` — all match in name and type. One nuance: `pipeline-run.sh:846` lets the string `"none"` through as a phase `verdict` (`gate_verdict` returns `none` at :872/:874 and only `"null"`/`""` are nulled); the row copies it verbatim (:291) and `--validate` does not check phase verdicts.

**11. Minor**
- `:332` `9>>"$OUT.lock"` leaves a permanent `runs.jsonl.lock` beside the output. Low.
- Arm precedence matches the header (manifest > meta/arm > pipeline.json; refusal only on manifest≠meta/arm). A manifest that disagrees with pipeline.json's own `arm` when `meta/arm` is absent is silently accepted (verified: arm=`a0_bare`), but pipeline-run.sh always writes `meta/arm` (:290), so this is informational.
- regen.sh output is non-deterministic (fresh `git init` commit as `source_commit`, host fingerprint as `image_digest`, timestamps, `$$-$RANDOM` session ids), so every regeneration produces a diff; the tests don't depend on those values.
- regen.sh:88's `git check-ignore` pruning depends on the repo's `.gitignore` (not in the PR); the generated tree contains `*.log` and `sandbox/.loa.config.yaml`, which the comment says are ignored — unverified.

## Clean areas
`set -euo pipefail` interactions (`jq -e` inside `||`/`if`, the `&&` at :184) are correct; `--attempts` regex guard works (`007`→7, `0`→0); every documented option exists and `--help` works; the `--validate` read loop handles blank lines, missing trailing newline and reports correct line numbers; MODELINV line-range join (`modelinv_lines.from/to`) and tab handling (:195-197) are correct; `norm_model` region-prefix stripping behaves as tested; `zone_violations` path regex and transcript naming (`events-<label>.jsonl`, pipeline-run.sh:641) match; `voices()` and degraded-cause logic match the header's four causes; MANIFEST.json `arm_map` keys match the ten `--run-id` values regen.sh passes and `suite.yaml` matches what regen passes as `--suite-file`.

I have what I need; no further requests. Here is the review.

## Test runs

Scratch copy: `/workspace/pr/head` → `$HOME/scratch-head.SvKFSf` (note: `/tmp` is mounted `noexec` here, so bats cannot exec scripts under `/tmp`; also the snapshot dropped the exec bits that the diff declares as `100755`, so I `chmod +x`'d the scripts — both are environment artifacts, not PR defects).

- `bash -n` on spend.sh, took-effect.sh, run-arms.sh, fingerprint.sh, freeze.sh, validate-suite.sh, execute-agent.sh, claude-ablation-stub.sh, suite-lib.bash, regen.sh: all OK. shellcheck is not installed.
- `bats evals/tests/spend.bats`: **6/6 pass**.
- `bats evals/tests/took-effect.bats`: fails in `setup()` on a fresh copy of the PR because `evals/tests/fixtures/ablation-runs/runs/` does not exist (see finding 1). After running `regen.sh` (which works from the files in the PR): **21/21 pass**.
- Not runnable from the PR snapshot: `run-arms.bats`, `arm-toggles.bats` (need `evals/fixtures/review-prs`, `sandbox.sh`, `grade.sh`, `compare.sh`, `claude-stub.sh`, `.claude/scripts/*` — not in the diff), `freeze.bats`, `validate-suite.bats` (need `grimoires/loa/evals/ablation-2.0/smoke/*` and `.claude/scripts/compat-lib.sh`). I reviewed those by reading.

## Findings

1. **`head/evals/tests/took-effect.bats:18`** — severity high, confidence high. The fixture run directories the test copies are not in the PR: the diff (72 files) contains `fixtures/ablation-runs/{MANIFEST.json,regen.sh,suite.yaml,prs/,tasks/}` but no `runs/`; `setup()` does `cp -a "$FX/runs" "$T/runs"` and every test errors out (`ablation-row.bats` has the same dependency). CI (`.github/workflows/bats-tests.yml:221`, `bats evals/tests/`) does not call `regen.sh`, and `regen.sh:7-8` says the runs are meant to be tracked. Either commit `runs/` or regenerate in `setup_file`.
   `cp -a "$FX/runs" "$T/runs"`

2. **`head/evals/harness/took-effect.sh:266`** — severity high, confidence high (reproduced). `integrity_clean` never fails when the sandbox `checksums.json` differs from the recorded `arm_evidence.manifest_sha256` (which `lib/sandbox-mount.sh:418` sets to the sha256 of checksums.json at mount time); the comparison is decorative. I appended text to `sandbox/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md`, regenerated checksums.json, and got `integrity_clean OK 5 manifest entries verified; manifest_sha256 8c267cb13e8a` / `arm a1_full: OK`. Anyone (the agent under test included) who rewrites the manifest alongside the file defeats the rule; the PR's own test at `took-effect.bats:167-171` relies on exactly this gap. The mismatch should be a FAIL.
   `[[ "$filesha" == "$msha" ]] && EVID="$EVID (matches checksums.json)"`

3. **`head/evals/harness/took-effect.sh:254`** — severity medium, confidence high (reproduced). The hash walk only iterates manifest entries, so a file added under `sandbox/.claude/` that is not in the manifest (I added `.claude/hooks/injected.sh`) still yields `integrity_clean OK`. The header (`:34-35`) is honest about this, but "integrity_clean" on a mount with an injected hook/skill is misleading evidence; walk the tree and flag unlisted files (regen_sandbox_manifest excludes only `overrides/` and `checksums.json`, so the set is well defined).
   `for rel, want in sorted(files.items()):`

4. **`head/evals/harness/took-effect.sh:173-178`** — severity medium, confidence high (reproduced). `no_flatline_rows` passes when `eval/model-invoke.jsonl` does not exist at all (`n` stays 0): deleting the file from the a5 fixture gives `no_flatline_rows OK no flatline MODELINV rows; sprint.md present`. A run whose MODELINV capture failed or was never written is indistinguishable from a run where flatline was off. The sibling rules (`no_system_prompt:118`, `enforce_env_false:167`) correctly FAIL on "no evidence captured"; this one should too.
   `if [[ -f "$R/eval/model-invoke.jsonl" ]]; then`

5. **`head/evals/harness/run-arms.sh:454`** — severity medium, confidence high. On a transport-classified failure the first attempt's `executor.json` is discarded (`executor='null'`) before the retry, and `collect` (`:506`) reads cost only from the row's final `.executor.total_cost_usd`. A trial that times out (exit 124 is classified transport at `:401`) after spending close to `run_cap` has that spend dropped from `SPENT`, so `--max-usd` can be exceeded by one `run_cap` per retried trial; the header (`:18-19`) claims spent is the total of completed and failed rows. The attempt-1 executor.json is kept in artifacts (`:452`) but never summed.
   `ws=""; executor='null'`

6. **`head/evals/harness/spend.sh:135-141`** — severity medium, confidence high (reproduced). Dedup keeps the *first* row per `run_id` regardless of whether it carries a cost, and it dedups inside a single file too (the header `:18` only promises cross-file dedup). Input `{"run_id":"x1","status":"completed"}` followed by `{"run_id":"x1","cost_usd":9}` yields `runs_usd` 0 with `runs_rows_deduped: 1` — a start/finish or retry re-emission of a run row silently zeroes its cost. Prefer the max/last cost per run_id, or at least do not let a cost-less row claim the id.
   `if key is not None and key in seen:`

7. **`head/evals/harness/spend.sh:129`, `:152`** — severity low, confidence high. A row with no `cost_usd` (or `cost_micro_usd`) is counted as a normal row at zero cost with no stderr note and no counter — `SP-4:64` even asserts `ledger_rows` = 3 for a cost-less ledger row. A cost field that a writer forgot is invisible in the cap report. Also a negative `cost_usd` is accepted (`runs_usd: -5`, `headroom` above the cap).
   `c = float(r.get("cost_usd") or 0)`

8. **`head/evals/harness/spend.sh:49`, `:55`, `:56`** — severity low, confidence high (reproduced). `--since`, `--cap`, `--reserve` as the last argument hit `shift 2` with one arg left; under `set -e` the script exits 1 (bash "shift count out of range"), not the documented usage exit 2 (`:31`). `--cap` with no value → `exit=1`. Same pattern in `took-effect.sh:69-72` and `run-arms.sh:94-109` (pre-existing there), and `fingerprint.sh:44-46` uses `${2:?…}` which also exits 1 against its "2 usage error" contract (`:28`).
   `--cap) CAP="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;`

9. **`head/evals/harness/took-effect.sh:133`** — severity low, confidence high. `all_phases_present` accepts a phase-prefix for status `running`, which the header (`:17-19`) does not list; a run whose pipeline died before writing a terminal status (pipeline.json still says `running`) passes as if it were a legitimate early stop.
   `cap_failure|agent_error|interrupted|running)`

10. **`head/evals/suites/ablation-2.0.yaml:59`** / `took-effect.sh:112-121` — severity low, confidence high. `no_system_prompt` is listed as A0 evidence, but `pipeline-run.sh` never passes `--append-system-prompt-file` for any arm (grep: only `:61-62`, `:652-654` build argv; no such flag), so the rule is satisfied by every pipeline run and discriminates nothing; the a0 fixture's `OK … in 1 argv` is vacuous. Only `no_dot_claude` actually distinguishes A0.
    `took_effect: [no_dot_claude, no_system_prompt, no_audit_rows, integrity_clean]`

11. **`head/evals/harness/run-arms.sh:121`** — severity low, confidence high. `--max-usd 0.0` (or `0.00`) passes validation (`usd_ok` accepts it and only the literal `"0"` is rejected), then `budget_gate` cuts before trial 1: a batch directory, MANIFEST and a `partial` STATUS with zero trials are created, exit 1 instead of the usage refusal RA-10 expects for `0`.
    `usd_ok "$MAX_USD" && [[ "$MAX_USD" != "0" ]] || die …`

12. **`head/evals/tests/run-arms.bats:178`, `:221`** — severity low, confidence medium. RA-6 asserts `spend.run_cap_usd == 12` and RA-9's whole schedule assumes `run_cap` 12, but `run-arms.sh:123` reads the default from the live repo's `.loa.config.yaml` (`evals.ablation.run_cap_usd`). Neither test passes `--run-cap 12`, so the tests break the moment an operator sets that key (the PR header text says the key is the intended configuration point). I could not see the repo's config to confirm its current value.
    `[ "$(jq -r '.spend.run_cap_usd' "$B/MANIFEST.json")" = "12" ]`

13. **`head/evals/harness/freeze.sh:69`** — severity low, confidence high. `find "$d" -type f` skips symlinks, so a symlinked file under `tasks/` (e.g. `hidden/tests/x.py -> /elsewhere`) is never hashed, while `validate-suite.sh` (`os.path.isfile`, which follows links) accepts it; the frozen manifest then cannot detect changes to that content.
    `( cd "$ROOT" && find "$d" -type f -print )`

## Areas checked and found clean

- spend.sh arithmetic: micro-USD → USD division, `round(...,4)`/int collapse, `ts()` for date-only, `Z`, offsets and fractional seconds (Python 3.11), `>=` since-inclusive filter, `${RUNS[@]+…}` empty-array handling, unreadable-file exit 1 — all behave as documented (verified by probes).
- run-arms.sh budget math: `fadd`/`%.10g`, `tonumber? // 0` precedence, `budget_gate` wait-vs-cut logic reproduces RA-6/RA-9's expected sequences on paper; `aggregate_status` excludes `screen-*`; `cuts` aggregation correct.
- took-effect.sh: `expected_labels` jq (`and`/`!=` precedence, `//` fallbacks) matches the suite's `phases`/`phase_sets` and the fixture labels; env captures are strings so `// "unset"` is safe; awk frontmatter scan handles no-frontmatter and body `effort:`; batch `find … -exec test -f '{}/…'` works on GNU and BSD find.
- Suite consistency: arm ids, toggle names, `absent: true`, `phase_sets`, `caps {1500,12,250}`, `predicates` key order and `task_types` agree across `ablation-2.0.yaml`, the fixture `suite.yaml`, `resolve_arm_toggles` (arms[] then ab.arms[]), execute-agent.sh (`sprint_plan`/`context_resets` → exit 2, `loa_mount:false` drops the system-prompt flag, arm `effort` overrides), took-effect.sh and AT-13's yq assertions (ran them: all return the asserted values).
- validate-suite.sh: field checks, `rel_ok`, allowlist, mount-owned dest, leak regexes and exit codes line up with validate-suite.bats expectations; the `|| { …; die }` crash path is sound.
- fingerprint.sh: sorted `tool=version` lines, `absent`/`unknown` handling, jq `capture` program — fine.

## Could not verify

- Whether `grimoires/loa/evals/ablation-2.0/smoke/*`, `MANIFEST.sha256`, `.claude/scripts/compat-lib.sh`, `evals/suites/review-recall.yaml` and the review-prs corpus in the real repo match what `suite-lib.bash`, `freeze.bats` FZ-6, `validate-suite.bats` VS-1/VS-3 (defect id `D01-decoy-flag-reanchor`) and `run-arms.bats` assume.
- Whether `claude-stub.sh` honours `STUB_EVENTS_FILE` as `claude-ablation-stub.sh:32` requires.
- Whether `run-ablation.sh` (Sprint 259) will write to spend.sh's default paths (`grimoires/loa/reports/ablation-2.0/runs.jsonl`, `evals/results/ablation-2.0/*/rows.jsonl`); nothing in this PR writes them.

- `bash -n` on spend.sh, took-effect.sh, run-arms.sh, fingerprint.sh, freeze.sh, validate-suite.sh, execute-agent.sh, claude-ablation-stub.sh, suite-lib.bash, regen.sh: all OK. shellcheck is not installed.
- `bats evals/tests/spend.bats`: **6/6 pass**.
- `bats evals/tests/took-effect.bats`: fails in `setup()` on a fresh copy of the PR because `evals/tests/fixtures/ablation-runs/runs/` does not exist (see finding 1). After running `regen.sh` (which works from the files in the PR): **21/21 pass**.
- Not runnable from the PR snapshot: `run-arms.bats`, `arm-toggles.bats` (need `evals/fixtures/review-prs`, `sandbox.sh`, `grade.sh`, `compare.sh`, `claude-stub.sh`, `.claude/scripts/*` — not in the diff), `freeze.bats`, `validate-suite.bats` (need `grimoires/loa/evals/ablation-2.0/smoke/*` and `.claude/scripts/compat-lib.sh`). I reviewed those by reading.

## Findings

1. **`head/evals/tests/took-effect.bats:18`** — severity high, confidence high. The fixture run directories the test copies are not in the PR: the diff (72 files) contains `fixtures/ablation-runs/{MANIFEST.json,regen.sh,suite.yaml,prs/,tasks/}` but no `runs/`; `setup()` does `cp -a "$FX/runs" "$T/runs"` and every test errors out (`ablation-row.bats` has the same dependency). CI (`.github/workflows/bats-tests.yml:221`, `bats evals/tests/`) does not call `regen.sh`, and `regen.sh:7-8` says the runs are meant to be tracked. Either commit `runs/` or regenerate in `setup_file`.
   `cp -a "$FX/runs" "$T/runs"`

2. **`head/evals/harness/took-effect.sh:266`** — severity high, confidence high (reproduced). `integrity_clean` never fails when the sandbox `checksums.json` differs from the recorded `arm_evidence.manifest_sha256` (which `lib/sandbox-mount.sh:418` sets to the sha256 of checksums.json at mount time); the comparison is decorative. I appended text to `sandbox/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md`, regenerated checksums.json, and got `integrity_clean OK 5 manifest entries verified; manifest_sha256 8c267cb13e8a` / `arm a1_full: OK`. Anyone (the agent under test included) who rewrites the manifest alongside the file defeats the rule; the PR's own test at `took-effect.bats:167-171` relies on exactly this gap. The mismatch should be a FAIL.
   `[[ "$filesha" == "$msha" ]] && EVID="$EVID (matches checksums.json)"`

3. **`head/evals/harness/took-effect.sh:254`** — severity medium, confidence high (reproduced). The hash walk only iterates manifest entries, so a file added under `sandbox/.claude/` that is not in the manifest (I added `.claude/hooks/injected.sh`) still yields `integrity_clean OK`. The header (`:34-35`) is honest about this, but "integrity_clean" on a mount with an injected hook/skill is misleading evidence; walk the tree and flag unlisted files (regen_sandbox_manifest excludes only `overrides/` and `checksums.json`, so the set is well defined).
   `for rel, want in sorted(files.items()):`

4. **`head/evals/harness/took-effect.sh:173-178`** — severity medium, confidence high (reproduced). `no_flatline_rows` passes when `eval/model-invoke.jsonl` does not exist at all (`n` stays 0): deleting the file from the a5 fixture gives `no_flatline_rows OK no flatline MODELINV rows; sprint.md present`. A run whose MODELINV capture failed or was never written is indistinguishable from a run where flatline was off. The sibling rules (`no_system_prompt:118`, `enforce_env_false:167`) correctly FAIL on "no evidence captured"; this one should too.
   `if [[ -f "$R/eval/model-invoke.jsonl" ]]; then`

5. **`head/evals/harness/run-arms.sh:454`** — severity medium, confidence high. On a transport-classified failure the first attempt's `executor.json` is discarded (`executor='null'`) before the retry, and `collect` (`:506`) reads cost only from the row's final `.executor.total_cost_usd`. A trial that times out (exit 124 is classified transport at `:401`) after spending close to `run_cap` has that spend dropped from `SPENT`, so `--max-usd` can be exceeded by one `run_cap` per retried trial; the header (`:18-19`) claims spent is the total of completed and failed rows. The attempt-1 executor.json is kept in artifacts (`:452`) but never summed.
   `ws=""; executor='null'`

6. **`head/evals/harness/spend.sh:135-141`** — severity medium, confidence high (reproduced). Dedup keeps the *first* row per `run_id` regardless of whether it carries a cost, and it dedups inside a single file too (the header `:18` only promises cross-file dedup). Input `{"run_id":"x1","status":"completed"}` followed by `{"run_id":"x1","cost_usd":9}` yields `runs_usd` 0 with `runs_rows_deduped: 1` — a start/finish or retry re-emission of a run row silently zeroes its cost. Prefer the max/last cost per run_id, or at least do not let a cost-less row claim the id.
   `if key is not None and key in seen:`

7. **`head/evals/harness/spend.sh:129`, `:152`** — severity low, confidence high. A row with no `cost_usd` (or `cost_micro_usd`) is counted as a normal row at zero cost with no stderr note and no counter — `SP-4:64` even asserts `ledger_rows` = 3 for a cost-less ledger row. A cost field that a writer forgot is invisible in the cap report. Also a negative `cost_usd` is accepted (`runs_usd: -5`, `headroom` above the cap).
   `c = float(r.get("cost_usd") or 0)`

8. **`head/evals/harness/spend.sh:49`, `:55`, `:56`** — severity low, confidence high (reproduced). `--since`, `--cap`, `--reserve` as the last argument hit `shift 2` with one arg left; under `set -e` the script exits 1 (bash "shift count out of range"), not the documented usage exit 2 (`:31`). `--cap` with no value → `exit=1`. Same pattern in `took-effect.sh:69-72` and `run-arms.sh:94-109` (pre-existing there), and `fingerprint.sh:44-46` uses `${2:?…}` which also exits 1 against its "2 usage error" contract (`:28`).
   `--cap) CAP="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;`

9. **`head/evals/harness/took-effect.sh:133`** — severity low, confidence high. `all_phases_present` accepts a phase-prefix for status `running`, which the header (`:17-19`) does not list; a run whose pipeline died before writing a terminal status (pipeline.json still says `running`) passes as if it were a legitimate early stop.
   `cap_failure|agent_error|interrupted|running)`

10. **`head/evals/suites/ablation-2.0.yaml:59`** / `took-effect.sh:112-121` — severity low, confidence high. `no_system_prompt` is listed as A0 evidence, but `pipeline-run.sh` never passes `--append-system-prompt-file` for any arm (grep: only `:61-62`, `:652-654` build argv; no such flag), so the rule is satisfied by every pipeline run and discriminates nothing; the a0 fixture's `OK … in 1 argv` is vacuous. Only `no_dot_claude` actually distinguishes A0.
    `took_effect: [no_dot_claude, no_system_prompt, no_audit_rows, integrity_clean]`

11. **`head/evals/harness/run-arms.sh:121`** — severity low, confidence high. `--max-usd 0.0` (or `0.00`) passes validation (`usd_ok` accepts it and only the literal `"0"` is rejected), then `budget_gate` cuts before trial 1: a batch directory, MANIFEST and a `partial` STATUS with zero trials are created, exit 1 instead of the usage refusal RA-10 expects for `0`.
    `usd_ok "$MAX_USD" && [[ "$MAX_USD" != "0" ]] || die …`

12. **`head/evals/tests/run-arms.bats:178`, `:221`** — severity low, confidence medium. RA-6 asserts `spend.run_cap_usd == 12` and RA-9's whole schedule assumes `run_cap` 12, but `run-arms.sh:123` reads the default from the live repo's `.loa.config.yaml` (`evals.ablation.run_cap_usd`). Neither test passes `--run-cap 12`, so the tests break the moment an operator sets that key (the PR header text says the key is the intended configuration point). I could not see the repo's config to confirm its current value.
    `[ "$(jq -r '.spend.run_cap_usd' "$B/MANIFEST.json")" = "12" ]`

13. **`head/evals/harness/freeze.sh:69`** — severity low, confidence high. `find "$d" -type f` skips symlinks, so a symlinked file under `tasks/` (e.g. `hidden/tests/x.py -> /elsewhere`) is never hashed, while `validate-suite.sh` (`os.path.isfile`, which follows links) accepts it; the frozen manifest then cannot detect changes to that content.
    `( cd "$ROOT" && find "$d" -type f -print )`

## Areas checked and found clean

- spend.sh arithmetic: micro-USD → USD division, `round(...,4)`/int collapse, `ts()` for date-only, `Z`, offsets and fractional seconds (Python 3.11), `>=` since-inclusive filter, `${RUNS[@]+…}` empty-array handling, unreadable-file exit 1 — all behave as documented (verified by probes).
- run-arms.sh budget math: `fadd`/`%.10g`, `tonumber? // 0` precedence, `budget_gate` wait-vs-cut logic reproduces RA-6/RA-9's expected sequences on paper; `aggregate_status` excludes `screen-*`; `cuts` aggregation correct.
- took-effect.sh: `expected_labels` jq (`and`/`!=` precedence, `//` fallbacks) matches the suite's `phases`/`phase_sets` and the fixture labels; env captures are strings so `// "unset"` is safe; awk frontmatter scan handles no-frontmatter and body `effort:`; batch `find … -exec test -f '{}/…'` works on GNU and BSD find.
- Suite consistency: arm ids, toggle names, `absent: true`, `phase_sets`, `caps {1500,12,250}`, `predicates` key order and `task_types` agree across `ablation-2.0.yaml`, the fixture `suite.yaml`, `resolve_arm_toggles` (arms[] then ab.arms[]), execute-agent.sh (`sprint_plan`/`context_resets` → exit 2, `loa_mount:false` drops the system-prompt flag, arm `effort` overrides), took-effect.sh and AT-13's yq assertions (ran them: all return the asserted values).
- validate-suite.sh: field checks, `rel_ok`, allowlist, mount-owned dest, leak regexes and exit codes line up with validate-suite.bats expectations; the `|| { …; die }` crash path is sound.
- fingerprint.sh: sorted `tool=version` lines, `absent`/`unknown` handling, jq `capture` program — fine.

## Could not verify

- Whether `grimoires/loa/evals/ablation-2.0/smoke/*`, `MANIFEST.sha256`, `.claude/scripts/compat-lib.sh`, `evals/suites/review-recall.yaml` and the review-prs corpus in the real repo match what `suite-lib.bash`, `freeze.bats` FZ-6, `validate-suite.bats` VS-1/VS-3 (defect id `D01-decoy-flag-reanchor`) and `run-arms.bats` assume.
- Whether `claude-stub.sh` honours `STUB_EVENTS_FILE` as `claude-ablation-stub.sh:32` requires.
- Whether `run-ablation.sh` (Sprint 259) will write to spend.sh's default paths (`grimoires/loa/reports/ablation-2.0/runs.jsonl`, `evals/results/ablation-2.0/*/rows.jsonl`); nothing in this PR writes them.

## Review: container pipeline executor slice

### Tests run

| Run | Setup | Result |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `/tmp/head-pipe`, system **jq 1.6** (Debian bookworm) | **12 pass / 40 fail** — every test that executes a phase fails |
| 2 | `$HOME` scratch copy, **jq 1.7.1** | **47 pass / 5 fail** (tests 46–50, all container-mode) |
| 3 | `/tmp` scratch, jq 1.7.1 | invalid: this sandbox mounts `/tmp` `noexec` (phase exited 126) — environment, not the PR |
| 4 | `/workspace/.eval/tmp` scratch (exec-capable, not under `/home/evaluser`), jq 1.7.1 | **52/52 pass** |

`bash -n` clean on pipeline-run.sh, execute-agent.sh, fingerprint.sh, both stubs, mount-lib-stub.sh. `shellcheck` is not installed. The real repo has `evals/harness/pipeline-run.sh`'s dependencies (`fingerprint.sh`, `lib/phase-prompts/`, `fixtures/mount-lib-stub.sh`, `fixtures/ablation-runs/suite.yaml`) all present in `pr/head`; nothing was missing. Runs 1 and 2's failures are explained by findings 1 and 9 below.

### Findings

**1. `head/evals/harness/pipeline-run.sh:702`, `:816`, `:881` (also `head/evals/harness/lib/sandbox-mount.sh:462`) — severity high, confidence high**
`label` is a reserved word in jq 1.6; `--arg label … '$label'` is a compile error ("unexpected label, expecting IDENT"). On any jq 1.6 host (Debian 12, Ubuntu 22.04, the ablation image's own jq) every phase aborts at the argv-capture step before the CLI runs, `set -e` fires, `on_exit` writes `infrastructure_error`, exit 2. Reproduced: 40/52 tests fail with jq 1.6, 52/52 pass with 1.7.1. CI (`ubuntu-latest`) has 1.7.1 so CI will not notice; the framework already uses `$label` in `.claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh:378`, so this is consistent with an unstated jq ≥ 1.7 requirement — but pipeline-run.sh's own tool check (`:167`) only tests `command -v jq`.
`jq -n --arg label "$label" --arg name "$name" …`

**2. `head/evals/harness/pipeline-run.sh:860-862` — severity medium, confidence high**
Docker-client failures (`docker run` exit 125 = daemon error / name clash, 126 / 127 = `python3`/`claude` missing in the image or not on the hardcoded container PATH) and host-shim `execvpe` failures (python exits 1) are classified `agent_error` (exit 1), counted against the arm by ablation-row, instead of `infrastructure_error`. Reproduced via stub: `STUB_EXIT_PLAN=127` → `{"status":"agent_error","reason":"phase PLAN exited 127"}`. Container mode has no pre-check that `claude` exists in the image (host mode does at `:426`).
`finish agent_error 1 "phase $label exited $rc"`

**3. `head/evals/tests/pipeline-run.bats:237, 332, 339, 391, 392, 394, 610, 652, 668, 669, 726` — severity medium, confidence high**
Bare `! grep …` statements that are not the last line of a `@test` (or sit inside a `for` loop) can never fail the test: bash exempts `!`-inverted commands from `set -e`/ERR. Verified empirically with bats 1.13 (`! true` mid-test → `ok`). Consequence: the leakage test (24) asserts nothing about `hidden`/defect keys/arm ids in prompts; the meta-boundary test (44) never checks the arm id is absent from sandbox/snapshots/transcripts; the A7 test never checks `effort:` was stripped; the container allowlist test never checks `GH_TOKEN`/`AKIAX` are absent; the bedrock test's `! grep -rqF "$tok" "$T/log" "$T/dlog"` (726) is a no-op. Lines 265, 466, 627, 682 (last statements) and 257/725 (with `|| …`) are effective. Use `run ! grep …` / `[ "$status" -ne 0 ]`.

# Mount-integrity slice (#1267) — review findings

## Findings

### 1. The new CI gate fails on this PR's own tree: tracked `.claude/` files change but `.claude/checksums.json` is not regenerated
- `head/.github/workflows/bats-tests.yml:177` / `:178` — `bash tools/check-manifest-paths.sh` / `bash tools/gen-checksums.sh --check`
- Severity: **high** (CI red for this PR and for every subsequent PR until someone regenerates). Confidence: **high** for the hash-drift half, **medium** for the untracked-path half.
- Scenario: the PR modifies at least 7 tracked, manifest-covered files (`model-config.yaml`, `check-loa.sh`, `preflight.sh`, `generated-model-maps.sh`, `CLAUDE.loa.md`, bridgebuilder dist) yet `.claude/checksums.json` is absent from `head.diff` (72 files, none is the manifest). `gen-checksums.sh --check` compares content hashes, so it must report `changed:` for those paths and exit 1. Observed in the scratch tree: `DRIFT — 10 path(s)` (9 `__pycache__/*.pyc` entries carried by the committed manifest — the very #1267 class — plus `changed: .claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md`); `tests/unit/check-manifest-paths.bats` **MP-6 fails** for the same 9 entries. After running `tools/gen-checksums.sh` once and committing, both gates, MP-6 and `fresh-mount-proof.sh` pass — the tools are self-consistent; the PR just doesn't ship the regenerated artefact.

### 2. `write_sandbox_grimoire` uses the jq keyword `label` as a variable → compile error on jq 1.6
- `head/evals/harness/lib/sandbox-mount.sh:462` — `jq -n --arg now "$now" --arg label "$label" --arg tid "$tid" '` and `:467` — `local_label: $label`
- Severity: **high** (every pipeline run that mounts Loa dies at materialisation with `write_sandbox_grimoire exited 2`). Confidence: **high** — reproduced directly: `jq: error: syntax error, unexpected label, expecting IDENT or __loc__` → `ERROR: write_sandbox_grimoire: ledger write failed`, rc=2, and a zero-byte `ledger.json` is left behind. jq 1.6 is the stock package on Ubuntu 22.04/Debian bookworm; jq 1.7 accepts keyword variable names. Same pattern (other slice) in `pipeline-run.sh:702/708, 816, 881–882`, which is why 39/52 `pipeline-run.bats` cases fail here. Rename the binding (e.g. `$lbl`).

### 3. `check_integrity` on a submodule mount can no longer detect a deleted or dangling link
- `head/.claude/scripts/check-loa.sh:75` — `elif [[ "$submodule_mount" == "true" && -f ".loa/${file}" ]]; then` / `:76` — `not_mounted=$((not_mounted + 1))`
- Severity: **medium**. Confidence: **high** (deterministic).
- Scenario: every manifest path by construction exists under `.loa/`, so on a submodule mount the `Missing` branch is unreachable: delete the symlink `.claude/scripts/check-loa.sh` (or let it dangle — `-f` is false on a dangling link) and the run prints `not-mounted: N` and exits 0; before this PR it reported `Missing:` and exited 1. The fresh mount shows 423 not-mounted paths, so a removed link is invisible in that count. `tests/unit/check-loa-mount-scope.bats` has no deleted-link case. Distinguish "never linked" from "linked then removed" using the mount's own link manifest (`MANIFEST_*_SYMLINKS` / `--check-symlinks` in `mount-submodule.sh`).

### 4. Workflow path filter does not cover the paths the new gate protects
- `head/.github/workflows/bats-tests.yml:49` (`pull_request: paths:` block, items at `:50–70`) and `:23` (push block)
- Severity: **medium**. Confidence: **high**.
- Scenario: the filter lists `.claude/scripts/**`, `.claude/defaults/**`, two specific skills, etc., but not `.claude/skills/**` (general), `.claude/commands/**`, `.claude/protocols/**`, `.claude/loa/**`, `.claude/rules/**`, `.claude/templates/**`, `.claude/agents/**`, `.claude/checksums.json`, `tools/gen-checksums.sh`, `tools/check-manifest-paths.sh`. A PR editing only `.claude/skills/foo/SKILL.md` without regenerating the manifest never triggers the gate; the next unrelated PR that does trigger it goes red with a drift it did not cause.

### 5. Trust-boundary claim in the lib header does not match two code paths
- `head/evals/harness/lib/sandbox-mount.sh:383` — `tool="${EVAL_PROMPT_TREE:-$_SM_REPO_ROOT}/tools/gen-checksums.sh"` / `:386` — `"$tool" --root "$ws"`; and `:513` — `PROJECT_ROOT="$ws" bash "$ubs" --opt-out …` (where `ubs="$ws/.claude/scripts/beads/update-beads-state.sh"`, `:511`)
- Severity: **medium** (host-side execution of code from the tree under evaluation). Confidence: **medium** (depends on eval.yml deployment, not in this snapshot).
- Scenario: lines 75–77/97–100 assert the harness never runs `.claude/` code. (a) `gen-checksums.sh` from the prompt tree sources `<prompt tree>/.claude/scripts/compat-lib.sh` (`head/tools/gen-checksums.sh:51`), so when reached the harness executes PR-controlled shell. Unreachable via `pipeline-run.sh` (`.claude/` is excluded and the base commit precedes the mount), reachable via `execute-agent.sh` only if WORKSPACE tracks `.claude`. (b) `init_sandbox_beads` runs the sandbox's copy of `update-beads-state.sh` whenever `br` is not on PATH (typical in CI) — the sandbox `.claude/` is the PR's tree, executed on the host before the container executor starts. The `pipeline-run.bats` "trust boundary" test only scans `source` lines, so `bash <.claude path>` passes it.

### 6. `check-manifest-paths.sh` and `gen-checksums.sh` disagree on non-ASCII filenames
- `head/tools/check-manifest-paths.sh:80` — `git -C "$ROOT" ls-files -- .claude | sort -u > "${TMP_DIR}/tracked"` vs `head/tools/gen-checksums.sh:102` — `git -C "$ROOT" ls-files -z -- .claude | sort -z`
- Severity: **low–medium** (misleading CI red). Confidence: **high** — reproduced: a tracked `.claude/résumé.md` → `gen-checksums --check: OK`, `check-manifest-paths: FAIL … [other] 1 path(s): .claude/résumé.md` (git C-quotes it as `".claude/r\303\251sum\303\251.md"` under default `core.quotePath`). Use `-z | tr '\0' '\n'` or `-c core.quotePath=off`.

### 7. Stub diverges from the contract it claims to mirror, and a test asserts the stub-only value
- `head/evals/tests/fixtures/mount-lib-stub.sh:24` — `echo "mount=whole_tree"` vs real lib `head/evals/harness/lib/sandbox-mount.sh:134` — `_sm_evidence mount "tree"` (contract `:20`); `head/evals/tests/pipeline-run.bats:245` asserts `= whole_tree`.
- Severity: **low**. Confidence: **high**.
- Also: stub `:59` `effort_stripped=` vs lib `:347` `effort_skills_stripped`; stub `:30` reads only `.arms[]` and refuses an undeclared `baseline` (lib `:172` returns `{}`); stub `:21` `cp -a "$tree/.claude" "$ws/.claude"` nests `.claude/.claude` if the workspace already has one (lib uses `cp -a …/.claude/. …/.claude/`). The pipeline test therefore passes against evidence the real library never emits.

### 8. "Outside a git repository" tests depend on the temp dir not being inside a repo
- `head/tests/unit/gen-checksums.bats:89` — `run --separate-stderr bash "$GEN" --root "$T/plain" --check` (expects 2); `head/tests/unit/check-manifest-paths.bats:101` — `run bash "$CMP" --root "$T/plain" --manifest …` (expects 2)
- Severity: **low**. Confidence: **high** — observed: with `TMPDIR` under the checkout (`/workspace/.eval/tmp`) both fail (`gen-checksums` exits 1 "manifest not found", `check-manifest-paths` exits 1 "untracked"); with `TMPDIR=/tmp` both pass. Set `GIT_CEILING_DIRECTORIES="$T"` in the test.

### 9. `cp -P` without `-R` follows symlinks on macOS
- `head/tools/fresh-mount-proof.sh:129` — `cp -P "$SRC/$p" "$UP/$p"`
- Severity: **low** (dev tool; CI is ubuntu-only). Confidence: **medium**. BSD `cp -P` only takes effect with `-R`; a `--worktree` overlay on macOS turns tracked symlinks into regular files in the proof clone.

### 10. Header references a test that does not exist
- `head/tests/unit/gen-checksums.bats:8`–`9` — "the live manifest is only read by GC-8" — there is no GC-8; this file never reads the live manifest.
- Severity: **low**. Confidence: **high**.

## Verified clean
- `.claude/defaults/model-config.yaml.checksum` = sha256 of head `model-config.yaml` (`ba767f53…`); base pair also consistent.
- `dist/.build-manifest.json` sha256 entries for `config.generated.ts` and `truncation.generated.ts` match the head files; `.ts`/`.js` registry, reasoning and token-budget entries for `gpt-6.1-sol` are identical; `generated-model-maps.sh` passes `gen-adapter-maps.sh --check` ("matches YAML"); `test_pricing_resolution_ladder.py` (15 passed) and `test_model_registry_parity.py` (6 passed) pass against head.
- `CLAUDE.loa.md` header: body identical to base; `marker-utils.sh update-hash` reproduces `a7a0470c…` exactly, so leaving the hash unchanged while bumping `version: 2.0.0-rc.5` is correct; `.loa-version.json` agrees.
- `check-loa.sh`: the added `return 0` fixes a latent `set -e` exit when the function's last `&&` list failed. `preflight.sh` symlink resolution matches `mount-submodule.sh`'s per-file link of `.claude/checksums.json`.
- `bash -n` clean on all 8 shell files; `shellcheck` not installed.

## Tests run (scratch copy = `/workspace/.claude` base tree + `pr/head` overlay, `git init`, `__pycache__` ignored)
- `tests/unit/check-loa-mount-scope.bats`: 6/6 pass.
- `tests/unit/check-manifest-paths.bats`: 5/7 → MP-6 (stale manifest, finding 1), MP-7 (finding 8); MP-6 passes after regeneration, MP-7 passes with `TMPDIR=/tmp`.
- `tests/unit/gen-checksums.bats`: 6/7 → GC-7 (finding 8); passes with `TMPDIR=/tmp`.
- `tools/fresh-mount-proof.sh --ref HEAD`: setup and offline mount work (112 link lines); rc=0 with `Tampered=0 Missing=0 not-mounted=423` once the manifest is regenerated and the tree is on an exec-capable filesystem.
- `evals/tests/arm-toggles.bats` (real lib): AT-9, AT-10, AT-16, AT-20 pass; the other 20 need fixtures absent from the frozen head (`evals/tests/fixtures/claude-stub.sh`, `evals/suites/review-recall.yaml`, `grimoires/loa/evals/ablation-2.0/smoke/*`) — not verifiable here.
- `evals/tests/pipeline-run.bats` (stub lib): 13/52 pass; the failures are the jq-1.6 `$label` error in `pipeline-run.sh` (same class as finding 2).

## Could not verify
- The real upstream base `.claude/checksums.json` (not in `pr/base`); `/workspace/.claude` is a near-head snapshot whose manifest already carries head hashes, so the exact drift list in CI will differ from what I observed, but non-zero drift is certain.
- `eval.yml` trust-boundary scan rules (not in snapshot) for finding 5.
- Source-map (`.map`) consistency beyond being single-line JSON; `.build-manifest.json` `source_hash` (inputs unknown).
- Environment notes: `/tmp` is mounted `noexec` here and jq is 1.6; both were controlled for by relocating to `/workspace/.eval/tmp` and by direct reproduction respectively. `/workspace/pr/.run/audit.jsonl` is hook-generated audit output, not something I wrote; nothing under `/workspace/pr` was modified.

# `.run/`) that exist only on the generating machine end up in the manifest and
# read as Missing on every fresh mount. This generator lists
#

#    "files": {"<path>": "<sha256 hex>", ...}}

# the same tree are byte-identical except `generated`. The working-tree content
# of each tracked path is hashed (an unstaged edit is reflected); a tracked
# path deleted from the working tree is skipped with a warning on stderr.

# Sprint 1 Review Feedback

**Reviewer:** Senior Tech Lead Reviewer Agent
**Date:** 2026-10-22
**Sprint Reference:** grimoires/loa/sprint.md
**Implementation Report:** grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-1/reviewer.md (carries `pr/PR.md`; no `## AC Verification` section exists — in this evaluation layout the PR description stands in for the report, so that automatic rule is recorded as inapplicable rather than applied)

---

## Overall Assessment

The change under review is `pr/head.diff` (72 files): the #1267 mount-integrity fix (`check-loa.sh`, `preflight.sh`, `tools/gen-checksums.sh`, `tools/check-manifest-paths.sh`, `tools/fresh-mount-proof.sh` + unit tests), the `gpt-6.1-sol` catalog entry, and the cycle-130 ablation harness (`pipeline-run.sh`, `lib/sandbox-mount.sh`, `ablation-row.sh`, `took-effect.sh`, `spend.sh`, `run-arms.sh`, `freeze.sh`, `fingerprint.sh`, `validate-suite.sh`, `Dockerfile.ablation`, suite yaml, fixtures and bats).

The design is sound and much of it is careful: the secret path (`AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK` by name only, `<set>` in captures, fd-closing exec shim, exactly two mounts) held up under hand-tracing and under the 52 pipeline tests when run with jq 1.7.1; `pipeline.json` field names and types match what `ablation-row.sh` reads; the `model-config.yaml.checksum`, bridgebuilder `.build-manifest.json` hashes and `CLAUDE.loa.md` header hash all verify; the adapter pricing tests pass against head.

It cannot merge as is. Two of the PR's own new CI steps go red on this tree (the fixture run directories the row/took-effect tests copy are not in the PR; the integrity-manifest gate is added while the PR changes manifest-covered files without shipping a regenerated `.claude/checksums.json`). The harness uses jq 1.7-only syntax with no version check, and on jq 1.6 (Debian bookworm, Ubuntu 22.04, the ablation image's own jq) every mounted run dies at materialisation — reproduced here. Eleven negated `grep` assertions in `pipeline-run.bats`, including the secret-leak and arm-id leak checks, are bare `! grep` statements mid-test and cannot fail. The cross-model dissent (2/2 voices, consensus) raised one BLOCKING finding on the `preflight.sh` count rule.

Karpathy: `GOAL-DRIVEN:` the leak-guard and secret-leak tests do not fail when they break (H4). `SIMPLICITY[delete]:` dead `brbuild` Docker stage; `SIMPLICITY[shrink]:` the phase-plan jq is duplicated verbatim between `pipeline-run.sh` and `took-effect.sh`; `PRICE_CACHE` is populated only inside a subshell and never read. net: -25 lines possible. Complexity: `run_phase` is ~235 lines (`pipeline-run.sh:634-868`), `apply_arm_toggles` ~120 (`sandbox-mount.sh:255-374`), the row builder is one ~105-line jq program (`ablation-row.sh:224-327`) — all over the 50-line threshold without a justifying comment.

Test runs performed (scratch copies of `pr/head`; `/tmp` is `noexec` here so exec-capable scratch dirs were used): `spend.bats` 6/6; `took-effect.bats` setup fails on the shipped tree (no `runs/`), 21/21 after `regen.sh` under jq 1.7.1; `ablation-row.bats` 0/18 as shipped, 18/18 after regen under jq 1.7.1, 11/18 after regen under jq 1.6 (regen silently produced broken fixtures); `pipeline-run.bats` 12/52 under jq 1.6, 52/52 under jq 1.7.1; `check-loa-mount-scope.bats` 6/6; `check-manifest-paths.bats` 5/7 (MP-6 stale manifest, MP-7 TMPDIR); `gen-checksums.bats` 6/7 (GC-7 TMPDIR); `arm-toggles.bats`, `run-arms.bats`, `freeze.bats`, `validate-suite.bats` need repo fixtures absent from the frozen tree and were reviewed by reading. `bash -n` clean on every shell file; `shellcheck` not installed.

**Verdict:** CHANGES REQUIRED

---

## Changes Required

### 1. Testing — the new eval-harness CI step fails on this PR

- **HIGH** (confidence: high) `head/evals/tests/ablation-row.bats:19` — `cp -a "$FX/runs" "$T/runs"` in `setup()` copies `evals/tests/fixtures/ablation-runs/runs/`, which is not in the PR (72 files, none under `runs/`); every test in this file and in `head/evals/tests/took-effect.bats:18` errors in setup, so `bats --print-output-on-failure evals/tests/` (`head/.github/workflows/bats-tests.yml:221`) fails.
**File:** `head/evals/tests/ablation-row.bats:19`, `head/evals/tests/took-effect.bats:18`
**Issue:** `regen.sh:2-8` says the run directories are tracked fixtures, but they were never committed; no workflow step runs `regen.sh` first.
**Why This Matters:** 39 tests (18 + 21) that are the only coverage of `ablation-row.sh` and `took-effect.sh` cannot execute, and the CI job the PR adds is red from its first run.
**Required Fix:** Commit `evals/tests/fixtures/ablation-runs/runs/` (after fixing `regen.sh`, see Observations), or build the fixtures in `setup_file` and correct the bats headers that call them checked-in.

### 2. Testing — the new integrity-manifest gate fails on this PR

- **HIGH** (confidence: high) `head/.github/workflows/bats-tests.yml:178` — `bash tools/gen-checksums.sh --check` compares the committed `.claude/checksums.json` with a regeneration over the tracked tree; this PR edits manifest-covered tracked files (`model-config.yaml`, `check-loa.sh`, `preflight.sh`, `generated-model-maps.sh`, `CLAUDE.loa.md`, six bridgebuilder `dist/` and `resources/` files) and `head.diff` carries no `.claude/checksums.json`, so the check exits 1 (`head/tools/gen-checksums.sh:144-168`: absent manifest or drift are both exit 1).
**File:** `head/.github/workflows/bats-tests.yml:177-178`
**Issue:** The gate is introduced without the artefact it checks being regenerated in the same change. Observed on a scratch tree: `DRIFT — 10 path(s)`; `tests/unit/check-manifest-paths.bats` MP-6 fails on the same stale manifest. After one `tools/gen-checksums.sh` run both gates and MP-6 pass, so the tools themselves are self-consistent.
**Why This Matters:** Every PR after this one is blocked until someone regenerates the manifest, and the first red run is this PR's.
**Required Fix:** Run `tools/gen-checksums.sh` and commit `.claude/checksums.json` in this PR; consider making the gate's path filter and the regeneration step explicit (see Observations on `paths:`).

### 3. Portability — jq 1.7-only syntax with no version floor; every mounted run dies on jq 1.6

## Overall Assessment

The change under review is `pr/head.diff` (72 files): the #1267 mount-integrity fix (`check-loa.sh`, `preflight.sh`, `tools/gen-checksums.sh`, `tools/check-manifest-paths.sh`, `tools/fresh-mount-proof.sh` + unit tests), the `gpt-6.1-sol` catalog entry, and the cycle-130 ablation harness (`pipeline-run.sh`, `lib/sandbox-mount.sh`, `ablation-row.sh`, `took-effect.sh`, `spend.sh`, `run-arms.sh`, `freeze.sh`, `fingerprint.sh`, `validate-suite.sh`, `Dockerfile.ablation`, suite yaml, fixtures and bats).

The design is sound and much of it is careful: the secret path (`AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK` by name only, `<set>` in captures, fd-closing exec shim, exactly two mounts) held up under hand-tracing and under the 52 pipeline tests when run with jq 1.7.1; `pipeline.json` field names and types match what `ablation-row.sh` reads; the `model-config.yaml.checksum`, bridgebuilder `.build-manifest.json` hashes and `CLAUDE.loa.md` header hash all verify; the adapter pricing tests pass against head.

# Sprint 1 Review Feedback

**Reviewer:** Senior Tech Lead Reviewer Agent
**Date:** 2026-10-22
**Sprint Reference:** grimoires/loa/sprint.md
**Implementation Report:** grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-1/reviewer.md (carries `pr/PR.md`; no `## AC Verification` section exists — in this evaluation layout the PR description stands in for the report, so that automatic rule is recorded as inapplicable rather than applied)

---

## Overall Assessment

The change under review is `pr/head.diff` (72 files): the #1267 mount-integrity fix (`check-loa.sh`, `preflight.sh`, `tools/gen-checksums.sh`, `tools/check-manifest-paths.sh`, `tools/fresh-mount-proof.sh` + unit tests), the `gpt-6.1-sol` catalog entry, and the cycle-130 ablation harness (`pipeline-run.sh`, `lib/sandbox-mount.sh`, `ablation-row.sh`, `took-effect.sh`, `spend.sh`, `run-arms.sh`, `freeze.sh`, `fingerprint.sh`, `validate-suite.sh`, `Dockerfile.ablation`, suite yaml, fixtures and bats).

The design is sound and much of it is careful: the secret path (`AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK` by name only, `<set>` in captures, fd-closing exec shim, exactly two mounts) held up under hand-tracing and under the 52 pipeline tests when run with jq 1.7.1; `pipeline.json` field names and types match what `ablation-row.sh` reads; the `model-config.yaml.checksum`, bridgebuilder `.build-manifest.json` hashes and `CLAUDE.loa.md` header hash all verify; the adapter pricing tests pass against head.

It cannot merge as is. Two of the PR's own new CI steps go red on this tree (the fixture run directories the row/took-effect tests copy are not in the PR; the integrity-manifest gate is added while the PR changes manifest-covered files without shipping a regenerated `.claude/checksums.json`). The harness uses jq 1.7-only syntax with no version check, and on jq 1.6 (Debian bookworm, Ubuntu 22.04, the ablation image's own jq) every mounted run dies at materialisation — reproduced here. Eleven negated `grep` assertions in `pipeline-run.bats`, including the secret-leak and arm-id leak checks, are bare `! grep` statements mid-test and cannot fail. The cross-model dissent (2/2 voices, consensus) raised one BLOCKING finding on the `preflight.sh` count rule.

Karpathy: `GOAL-DRIVEN:` the leak-guard and secret-leak tests do not fail when they break (H4). `SIMPLICITY[delete]:` dead `brbuild` Docker stage; `SIMPLICITY[shrink]:` the phase-plan jq is duplicated verbatim between `pipeline-run.sh` and `took-effect.sh`; `PRICE_CACHE` is populated only inside a subshell and never read. net: -25 lines possible. Complexity: `run_phase` is ~235 lines (`pipeline-run.sh:634-868`), `apply_arm_toggles` ~120 (`sandbox-mount.sh:255-374`), the row builder is one ~105-line jq program (`ablation-row.sh:224-327`) — all over the 50-line threshold without a justifying comment.

Test runs performed (scratch copies of `pr/head`; `/tmp` is `noexec` here so exec-capable scratch dirs were used): `spend.bats` 6/6; `took-effect.bats` setup fails on the shipped tree (no `runs/`), 21/21 after `regen.sh` under jq 1.7.1; `ablation-row.bats` 0/18 as shipped, 18/18 after regen under jq 1.7.1, 11/18 after regen under jq 1.6 (regen silently produced broken fixtures); `pipeline-run.bats` 12/52 under jq 1.6, 52/52 under jq 1.7.1; `check-loa-mount-scope.bats` 6/6; `check-manifest-paths.bats` 5/7 (MP-6 stale manifest, MP-7 TMPDIR); `gen-checksums.bats` 6/7 (GC-7 TMPDIR); `arm-toggles.bats`, `run-arms.bats`, `freeze.bats`, `validate-suite.bats` need repo fixtures absent from the frozen tree and were reviewed by reading. `bash -n` clean on every shell file; `shellcheck` not installed.

**Verdict:** CHANGES REQUIRED

---

## Changes Required

### 1. Testing — the new eval-harness CI step fails on this PR

- **HIGH** (confidence: high) `head/evals/tests/ablation-row.bats:19` — `cp -a "$FX/runs" "$T/runs"` in `setup()` copies `evals/tests/fixtures/ablation-runs/runs/`, which is not in the PR (72 files, none under `runs/`); every test in this file and in `head/evals/tests/took-effect.bats:18` errors in setup, so `bats --print-output-on-failure evals/tests/` (`head/.github/workflows/bats-tests.yml:221`) fails.
**File:** `head/evals/tests/ablation-row.bats:19`, `head/evals/tests/took-effect.bats:18`
**Issue:** `regen.sh:2-8` says the run directories are tracked fixtures, but they were never committed; no workflow step runs `regen.sh` first.
**Why This Matters:** 39 tests (18 + 21) that are the only coverage of `ablation-row.sh` and `took-effect.sh` cannot execute, and the CI job the PR adds is red from its first run.
**Required Fix:** Commit `evals/tests/fixtures/ablation-runs/runs/` (after fixing `regen.sh`, see Observations), or build the fixtures in `setup_file` and correct the bats headers that call them checked-in.

### 2. Testing — the new integrity-manifest gate fails on this PR

- **HIGH** (confidence: high) `head/.github/workflows/bats-tests.yml:178` — `bash tools/gen-checksums.sh --check` compares the committed `.claude/checksums.json` with a regeneration over the tracked tree; this PR edits manifest-covered tracked files (`model-config.yaml`, `check-loa.sh`, `preflight.sh`, `generated-model-maps.sh`, `CLAUDE.loa.md`, six bridgebuilder `dist/` and `resources/` files) and `head.diff` carries no `.claude/checksums.json`, so the check exits 1 (`head/tools/gen-checksums.sh:144-168`: absent manifest or drift are both exit 1).
**File:** `head/.github/workflows/bats-tests.yml:177-178`
**Issue:** The gate is introduced without the artefact it checks being regenerated in the same change. Observed on a scratch tree: `DRIFT — 10 path(s)`; `tests/unit/check-manifest-paths.bats` MP-6 fails on the same stale manifest. After one `tools/gen-checksums.sh` run both gates and MP-6 pass, so the tools themselves are self-consistent.
**Why This Matters:** Every PR after this one is blocked until someone regenerates the manifest, and the first red run is this PR's.
**Required Fix:** Run `tools/gen-checksums.sh` and commit `.claude/checksums.json` in this PR; consider making the gate's path filter and the regeneration step explicit (see Observations on `paths:`).

### 3. Portability — jq 1.7-only syntax with no version floor; every mounted run dies on jq 1.6

- **HIGH** (confidence: high) `head/evals/harness/pipeline-run.sh:708` — `'{label: $label, name: $name, …'` uses the jq reserved word `label` as a variable; on jq 1.6 this is `syntax error, unexpected label, expecting IDENT`, the argv capture fails under `set -e`, `on_exit` records `infrastructure_error` and the run exits 2 before the CLI starts. Same construct at `:702` (`--arg label`), `:816/:826`, `:881-882`, in `head/evals/harness/lib/sandbox-mount.sh:462,467` (`write_sandbox_grimoire` → `ledger write failed`, zero-byte `ledger.json`), and `head/evals/harness/ablation-row.sh:285` (`{name, label, …}` shorthand, jq ≥ 1.7 only).
**File:** `head/evals/harness/pipeline-run.sh:708`
**Issue:** Reproduced here with the system jq 1.6: 40/52 `pipeline-run.bats` and 7/18 `ablation-row.bats` fail; `regen.sh` writes `infrastructure_error` fixtures and exits 0. The tool check at `pipeline-run.sh:167` only tests `command -v jq`. CI (`ubuntu-latest`, jq 1.7.1) will not notice; Debian bookworm (the `Dockerfile.ablation` base) and Ubuntu 22.04 ship 1.6.
**Why This Matters:** An operator on a 1.6 host loses an entire batch to `infrastructure_error` with a jq compile error as the only clue; the fixtures regenerated on such a host are silently wrong.
**Required Fix:** Rename the binding (`$lbl`) and write `"label": .label` in the shorthand, or enforce `jq --version` ≥ 1.7 in the tool checks of `pipeline-run.sh`, `ablation-row.sh`, `took-effect.sh` and `regen.sh`.

### 4. Testing — negated assertions that cannot fail (GOAL-DRIVEN)

- **HIGH** (confidence: high) `head/evals/tests/pipeline-run.bats:726` — `! grep -rqF "$tok" "$T/log" "$T/dlog"` is a bare negated command inside a `for` loop; bash exempts `!`-prefixed commands from errexit, so bats reports `ok` whether or not the Bedrock token appears in the logs. Same at `:237` (`PATH=/evil`), `:332` (`^effort:` still in SKILL.md), `:339` (`--effort`), `:391-392` and `:394` (the `hidden` / defect-key / arm-id leak scan of prompts and task-brief), `:610` (arm id in sandbox/snapshots/transcripts/eval), `:652`, `:668-669` (`GH_TOKEN|AKIAX|SSH_AUTH_SOCK` in the allowlisted env).
**File:** `head/evals/tests/pipeline-run.bats:726` (and the ten lines above)
**Issue:** Verified with bats 1.13: `! true` mid-test passes; only a `!` on the last line of a `@test` fails. The leak-guard (`pipeline-run.sh:488-520`), secret-handling (`:661-690`) and effort-strip paths therefore have no failing check, although hand-tracing found them correct today.
**Why This Matters:** Security guarantees the harness header advertises (no secret in any capture or log, no arm id or hidden path in the sandbox) are not protected by CI; a regression ships green.
**Required Fix:** Use `run ! grep …` / `[ "$status" -ne 0 ]`, or `! grep … || fail "…"` as `:257` and `:725` already do.

### 5. Integrity check — `git ls-files` counts deleted tracked files (dissent BLOCKING)

- **HIGH** (confidence: high) `head/.claude/scripts/preflight.sh:190` — `ACTUAL_COUNT=$(git -C "${MANIFEST_TREE}" ls-files -- .claude | …)` reads the index, so a tracked `.claude/` file deleted from the working tree (a removed hook, guard script or rule) leaves `ACTUAL_COUNT` unchanged and the count mismatch the previous `find` count detected is suppressed; `check-loa.sh` still reports it as `Missing`, so this is a weakening of preflight's own check rather than a total loss.
**File:** `head/.claude/scripts/preflight.sh:190-191`
**Issue:** Raised as BLOCKING by the cross-model dissent (2/2 voices). The `find` fallback at `:196` only runs when the tracked count is 0.
**Why This Matters:** Preflight's integrity signal is the one that runs before every skill; it now passes a tree with fence files deleted.
**Required Fix:** Filter to paths that exist (`git ls-files -- .claude | while read -r p; do [[ -e "$p" ]] && …`), or subtract `git ls-files --deleted -- .claude`.

---

## Observations

### 1. took-effect evidence

- **MEDIUM** (confidence: high) `head/evals/harness/took-effect.sh:266` — `[[ "$filesha" == "$msha" ]] && EVID="$EVID (matches checksums.json)"` only decorates: a sandbox whose `.claude/` file was altered and whose `checksums.json` was regenerated afterwards passes `integrity_clean` (reproduced: appended to `CLAUDE.loa.md`, regenerated the manifest, `arm a1_full: OK`). The recorded `arm_evidence.manifest_sha256` is computed and never enforced. The walk at `:254` also iterates manifest entries only, so an injected `.claude/hooks/x.sh` passes (the header at `:34-35` says so, but the rule's name promises more).
**Suggestion:** Make a manifest-hash mismatch a FAIL (or a separate `manifest_rewritten` evidence line the row marks degraded) and flag unlisted files under `sandbox/.claude/`.
**Benefit:** `integrity_clean` becomes the arm-confound detector DEC-0418 intends.

- **MEDIUM** (confidence: high) `head/evals/harness/took-effect.sh:173` — `if [[ -f "$R/eval/model-invoke.jsonl" ]]` lets `no_flatline_rows` pass when the MODELINV capture is missing entirely (deleting the file from the a5 fixture → `OK`); sibling rules (`:118`, `:167`) fail on "no evidence captured".
**Suggestion:** Treat an absent ledger as FAIL with evidence `no eval/model-invoke.jsonl`.

- **LOW** (confidence: high) `head/evals/harness/took-effect.sh:133` — `cap_failure|agent_error|interrupted|running)` accepts a phase prefix for `running`, which the header (`:17-19`) does not list; a driver that died before writing a terminal status passes as an early stop.

### 2. Pipeline executor status and robustness

- **MEDIUM** (confidence: high) `head/evals/harness/pipeline-run.sh:862` — `finish agent_error 1 "phase $label exited $rc"` books docker-client failures (125 daemon/name clash, 126/127 `python3`/`claude` absent from the image PATH) and host-shim `execvpe` failures as `agent_error`, which `ablation-row.sh` counts against the arm; container mode has no pre-check that `claude` exists in the image (host mode has one at `:426`). Reproduced with the stub: `STUB_EXIT_PLAN=127` → `status agent_error`. The docker allowlist at `:683` also omits `DOCKER_CERT_PATH`, `DOCKER_TLS_VERIFY`, `DOCKER_CONTEXT`, so a TLS/remote context fails the same way.
**Suggestion:** Map 125/126/127 (and a `result.subtype == "missing"` with zero events) to `infrastructure_error`; probe `docker run … claude --version` once before the first phase.

- **MEDIUM** (confidence: high) `head/evals/harness/pipeline-run.sh:634` — `run_phase()` runs to `:868` (~235 lines, launch + watchdog + parse + record + decide) with nesting past three levels; `apply_arm_toggles` (`head/evals/harness/lib/sandbox-mount.sh:255-374`) and the row builder's single jq program (`head/evals/harness/ablation-row.sh:224-327`) are in the same class. No justifying comment.
**Suggestion:** Split launch/watchdog, record and decide into functions; the recorded fields do not change.

- **LOW** (confidence: high) `head/evals/harness/pipeline-run.sh:595` — `PRICE_CACHE="$PRICE_CACHE$m"…` is appended inside `price_for`, which is only ever called as `prices="$(price_for "$model")"` (`:718`), so the cache lives in a subshell and "one lookup per model" (`:576`) is one `pricing.py` run per phase.

- **LOW** (confidence: high) `head/evals/harness/pipeline-run.sh:85` — header says the image pins "codex 0.137.0"; `head/evals/harness/Dockerfile.ablation:25` pins `CODEX_VERSION=0.162.1`. `:50` documents `index.json` keys as `IMPLEMENT|FIX1|FIX2` while `:788` lowercases them (`ablation-row.sh` reads the lowercase keys, so only the doc is wrong).

The review is complete and the feedback file is written and self-checked.

**Verdict: CHANGES_REQUIRED** for sprint-1 (the cycle-130 sprint-258 PR). Feedback is at `grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-1/engineer-feedback.md`, ending with a `LOA-VERDICT` trailer that `verdict-derive.sh` reports consistent (0 critical, 5 high, 16 medium, 17 low, 0 excluded, no violations).

**Blocking findings (high):**
- **Fixture directory missing.** `ablation-row.bats` and `took-effect.bats` copy `fixtures/ablation-runs/runs/`, which is not in the PR, so all 39 tests error in setup and the new CI step fails.
- **Manifest gate red on its own PR.** The PR adds `gen-checksums.sh --check` to CI while changing manifest-covered files without shipping a regenerated `.claude/checksums.json`.
- **jq 1.7-only syntax, no version floor.** `$label` as a jq variable and the `{name, label}` shorthand fail to compile on jq 1.6. Reproduced here: 40 of 52 pipeline tests fail, and every mounted run dies at materialisation.
- **Vacuous negated assertions.** Eleven bare `! grep` statements mid-test in `pipeline-run.bats` cannot fail, including the Bedrock-token and arm-id leak checks. Verified with bats 1.13.
- **Dissent BLOCKING.** The new `git ls-files` count in `preflight.sh` still counts tracked files deleted from the worktree. `check-loa.sh` still catches these as Missing, so I noted the mitigation.

**Notable observations** include a decorative manifest-hash comparison in `took-effect.sh`, docker-client failures booked as `agent_error`, retried spend dropped from the batch cap, a swallowed failure in the fixture generator, the unreachable Missing branch on submodule mounts, and an npm `ignore-scripts` hardening claim that never reaches the agent.

**Process notes.** The cross-model dissent ran with two voices in consensus and no rejected payloads. The reviewer report has no AC Verification section because the PR description stands in for it in this layout, which I recorded as inapplicable rather than applying the automatic rule. Session continuity is in `grimoires/loa/NOTES.md`, and the trajectory entry is logged. Nothing under `pr/` was modified.

result:
The review is complete and the feedback file is written and self-checked.

**Verdict: CHANGES_REQUIRED** for sprint-1 (the cycle-130 sprint-258 PR). Feedback is at `grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-1/engineer-feedback.md`, ending with a `LOA-VERDICT` trailer that `verdict-derive.sh` reports consistent (0 critical, 5 high, 16 medium, 17 low, 0 excluded, no violations).

**Blocking findings (high):**
- **Fixture directory missing.** `ablation-row.bats` and `took-effect.bats` copy `fixtures/ablation-runs/runs/`, which is not in the PR, so all 39 tests error in setup and the new CI step fails.
- **Manifest gate red on its own PR.** The PR adds `gen-checksums.sh --check` to CI while changing manifest-covered files without shipping a regenerated `.claude/checksums.json`.
- **jq 1.7-only syntax, no version floor.** `$label` as a jq variable and the `{name, label}` shorthand fail to compile on jq 1.6. Reproduced here: 40 of 52 pipeline tests fail, and every mounted run dies at materialisation.
- **Vacuous negated assertions.** Eleven bare `! grep` statements mid-test in `pipeline-run.bats` cannot fail, including the Bedrock-token and arm-id leak checks. Verified with bats 1.13.
- **Dissent BLOCKING.** The new `git ls-files` count in `preflight.sh` still counts tracked files deleted from the worktree. `check-loa.sh` still catches these as Missing, so I noted the mitigation.

**Notable observations** include a decorative manifest-hash comparison in `took-effect.sh`, docker-client failures booked as `agent_error`, retried spend dropped from the batch cap, a swallowed failure in the fixture generator, the unreachable Missing branch on submodule mounts, and an npm `ignore-scripts` hardening claim that never reaches the agent.

**Process notes.** The cross-model dissent ran with two voices in consensus and no rejected payloads. The reviewer report has no AC Verification section because the PR description stands in for it in this layout, which I recorded as inapplicable rather than applying the automatic rule. Session continuity is in `grimoires/loa/NOTES.md`, and the trajectory entry is logged. Nothing under `pr/` was modified.
